description: A finished, local, one-burn Earth-orbit design workbench. Choose an idealized or custom starting orbit, coast or scrub to a burn point, adjust transverse and radial delta-v with controls or a draggable vector, compare the resulting conic, execute the impulse, and undo maneuvers. The product includes precise orbital metrics, collision and escape warnings, time warp, camera controls, a maneuver ledger, and in-product model documentation.

architecture.runtime: Vanilla JavaScript, DOM, Canvas 2D, and local CSS; no additional dependencies or WebGL.
architecture.physics: Pure functions in physics.js, shared directly by the interface and numerical tests. Bracketed Newton universal-variable Kepler f/g propagation with stable Stumpff functions, orbital elements, local radial/transverse impulsive burns, anomaly-derived and numerically refined future surface crossings, and conic trajectory sampling.
architecture.state: In-memory only. Up to 12 executed burns with exact pre-burn state and draft restoration. No network calls, storage, cookies, accounts, parent/top access, or cross-frame communication.
architecture.packaging: index.html has exactly <script type="module" src="./main.js"></script>. All assets are local and Vite-bundleable for the opaque-origin allow-scripts iframe.

numericalAssumptions.units: Position km, velocity km/s, time seconds; user delta-v inputs m/s converted at the physics boundary.
numericalAssumptions.forceModel: Fixed, spherical Earth and negligible spacecraft mass; planar Newtonian two-body motion.
numericalAssumptions.maneuvers: Instantaneous impulse in the outward radial and transverse along-angular-momentum directions. Prograde is explicitly transverse and is not generally identical to velocity direction in eccentric motion.
numericalAssumptions.collision: Coasting stops at the first future radius=6371 km crossing. A negative mathematical periapsis altitude is exposed in the metrics.
numericalAssumptions.classification: Bound for specific energy < -1e-10 km^2/s^2; parabolic numerical neighbourhood for absolute specific energy <= 1e-10 km^2/s^2.
numericalAssumptions.display: Full safe closed ellipses; future arcs ending at impact for colliding conics; six-hour future arcs and coast limits for unbound conics. Display geometry has 320 intervals by default.
numericalAssumptions.interactionRanges: Initial periapsis/apoapsis altitudes 120–100,000 km, with apoapsis >= periapsis. Transverse delta-v -3,500 to +3,500 m/s, radial delta-v -2,500 to +2,500 m/s, 10 m/s increments. Time warp 1x, 10x, 100x, 1,000x.

limitations: No atmospheric drag, reentry heating, oblateness/J2, third bodies, Earth rotation, inclination, finite-duration thrust, fuel, spacecraft mass evolution, engine limits, relativistic effects, or live celestial data.
Presets are idealized states, not live spacecraft or actual mission ephemerides.
Unbound coast inspection is bounded to six hours; the maneuver ledger holds 12 impulses.
A very large near-parabolic bound ellipse can make Earth appear tiny in the fit-both-orbits view; zoom/pan and Fit controls are available.
Educational orbit-design intuition; not operational flight planning.
